name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.320.0 — The user reaches build: every seed journey opens with a job story and carries a first-run or empty beat (--mark seed-done refuses otherwise); the roadmap brief and every new spec carry a Users section that decision-lint requires (missing-users-section); build workers and the reviewer read it, the reviewer walks the flow cold; the wireframe binds structure, not looks; the unused UX research brief is retired. 7.319.0 — fanout-driver: a red main gate now outranks DISPATCH, so the next planned lane is never dispatched onto a red main after --mark merged (a pending question still relays first); --mark gate-repaired re-loads the state after the long gate run and applies only its outcome, so a --mark returned that landed meanwhile is no longer clobbered; merging a fix lane with a queueId ticks its queue item through spec-queue done (whatever the gate colour, since the work is on main), warning instead of dying when the tick fails; and a green gate-repaired drops that lane's 'main gate red' line from the queued list, so the report no longer lists a repair that no longer exists. 7.318.0 — fix(review): finishMerge keeps the review state where the merge-strategy mark finds it until merge-back.sh cleanup exits 0, and cleanup lifts the agent harness's own 'claude agent' worktree lock — a failed close cleanup is re-runnable.
